title: The currency control book scheme
summary: He takes currency control books from an officer and sends money orders home at three to one.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: In devious means. And selling some money orders.
A little black market and things like that? (LAUGHTER).
Yes. The reason I did that is some little, there was some little lieutenant there, I don't know whether I should tell these things?

Some little lieutenant in Remes, France. I get in and this guy had just come from America and hadn't seen any action or anything. A young guy and a smart alec and he was selling money orders to me, a lieutenant!. An officer, selling me money orders. He wanted to sell me money orders. Three hundred francs for one hundred dollars, in other words, three to one.

And by that time we had currency control books. Now whatever my salary was why that was the amount of money I could send home by American Express I mean, postal money orders I should say. And the same thing with anyone. Your currency control books, they call it.

So this guy is trying to sell me these money orders and inside I am burning up. But I went through with the deal with him, three to one. And he had a drawer full of currency control books, blanks, but official. So he made the error of stepping out of the office for a moment while I glommed onto (grabbed?) about thirty or forty of these books and put them in my pocket and took off.

Away you know, goodbye and so on and so forth. And he was a Special Service Officer you see. So I used to take these you know different places where we'd go in Germany, England and France and guys would come

back stage after we'd finish a show and they say, hey McPartland, how are you, you know. I saw you at the Sherman Hotel you know, with Fats Waller and his band and your band and all the different things and all the places and all. I'd say, wait a minute guys, three to one you know, currency control books.

I'd do it, I'd put on you know, Sergeant Plotsky or it didn't make any difference what the name was. Had that weapons carrier and go around to different what do you call it, post offices and get money orders for the guys. Three to one. So I'd send them home to myself under a different name.

Joe Franco or something like that. You know. Sergeant Joe Franco to Jimmy McPartland made out. So I came out with a fairly good size sum. So, I probably shouldn't tell that since it's not a nice thing to do. But this officer burned me up.
